label: Sky Walker
summary: With the Leap Stone (renamed Sky Walker) Alucard can jump again in midair any number of times, and the dive kick moves to Up+Triangle during any jump.

edits.why: func_8010FDF8 (jump-input checker) Leap Stone branch: lhu g_Player.unk44 -> ori v0,zero,4, so the "already double-jumped" bit (unk44&1) always reads 0 -> unlimited midair jumps with Leap Stone
PlayerStepJump dive-kick block: remove "return if not double-jumping" (beqz -> nop), dive kick available in any jump
dive kick held button PAD_DOWN (0x4000) -> PAD_UP (0x1000)
dive kick tapped button PAD_CROSS (0x40) -> PAD_TRIANGLE (0x10)

vanilla.reason: Four instruction words in DRA player-control code; vanilla bytes equal the off bytes and nothing else is referenced.

overlaps.detail: No byte overlap (wolf edit is DRA 0x8EABE). The reverted SOTN-Single-High-Jump PPFs touched 0x6EA40/0x704D0 and a cave at 0x42600; both are reverted in a and do not overlap these words.
No byte overlap; Up+Triangle is not used by the L2 shortcuts or subweapon controls.

optionalTextEdits.why: Leap Stone description "Wearer can do double jump" -> "Jump anywhere in midair  "

notes: ASS 1.3.0/1.3.1 base feature (v->o, unchanged o->a). The double-jump branch in the jump-input checker (6FDF8.c: branchFlags&0x20 && IsRelicActive(LEAP_STONE) && padTapped&CROSS && !(g_Player.unk44&1)) now loads the constant 4 instead of g_Player.unk44, so the test always passes. In vanilla the dive kick (PlayerStepJump, 71830.c) needs a double jump in progress and Down+Cross; ASS removes the requirement and remaps it to Up+Triangle because Cross now always jumps again. The adjacent v->o change at DRA 0x773C8 (Wingsmash timer decrement removed = infinite Wingsmash) is a separate ASS feature and is not included. Relic text (name 'Sky Walker', description 'Jump anywhere in midair') differs from vanilla in DRA and SEL; it is listed under optionalTextEdits but left out of edits because the stats editor owns item/relic text. Same lengths as the vanilla strings, so toggling the text is safe if wanted. RIC.BIN has no jump-related change.
